publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.2 fixes erasing a person whose agent has worked in Uptime. Erasing a member now also removes their name from what their agents did: the changes saved for them, their acknowledgements and assignments in an incident's history, the agent door's records of their agents, and their drill consents and schedules; notification sends an agent prepared for them are removed. An agent's work is now recorded under the agent's own identifier, not its sponsor's name, in the audit, in an alert route's change history and in an incident's timeline. The owner's archive export and backup no longer fail with Invalid anonymized archive audit once an agent has acted. Older agent lines carried the sponsor's name; migration 0087 rewrites them, so after upgrading, older agent lines in an incident timeline read Agent legacy, and the earlier name cannot be recovered from Uptime. A company's agent can also schedule alert-destination drills: a company owner consents under Settings › Alerts, Scheduled drills, to a window, an interval and count, a confirmation wait, a route owner and a USD phone budget, and the agent schedules bounded email, Slack or default webhook drills, with the provider's acknowledgment kept apart from the recipient's confirmation, reminders to the internal route owner and a proposed correction that changes nothing until a person applies it. Phone calls and custom webhook templates are not available for scheduled drills. Two additive migrations (0086 and 0087), no new required settings, and @runeditrun/rer is pinned to exactly 0.2.96. Back up before upgrading, because 0087 changes stored audit labels; monitors, history, incidents, destinations and private settings are kept. Known issue: a response body over 64 KiB still fails the check, so monitor a smaller page such as a health endpoint. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0, 0.5.1 and 0.5.2. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png
